name: MMX
tagline: JAXA's Phobos sample-return spacecraft, carrying the CNES/DLR rover Idefix
description: MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) is JAXA's mission to Phobos, the larger of Mars's two moons, and the first planned sample return from the Martian system. Mitsubishi Electric built the spacecraft: three modules (propulsion, exploration and return) with a launch mass of 4,480 kg, standing 5.3 m high, 4.5 m deep and 9.0 m wide in JAXA's figures. It launched on H3 flight 10 from Tanegashima at 19:41 UTC on 2026-10-19 (20 October in Japan), and on 2026-10-21 JAXA confirmed that its first critical operations, including deploying the solar array paddles, were complete. MMX is due to reach the Martian system in 2027, enter a quasi-satellite orbit around Phobos and make two landings. The first is Idefix, a 25 kg rover built by DLR and CNES, which is to drive on the surface for about 100 days around the turn of 2028/2029. The main spacecraft then lands to collect at least 10 g of surface material, observes Deimos, leaves in 2030 and releases its return capsule for recovery in Australia in 2031.
best_known_for: Aims to bring back the first sample from the Martian system, taken from the moon Phobos
